report.source_text: Angiography findings revealed irregularities in the diameter of the right gastric artery (Figure 3). While the angiogram did not reveal any aneurysms or active bleeding (Figure 3), coil embolization of the right gastric artery was performed due to vessel irregularities and compelling indications of structural damage, along with the potential for rebleeding or pseudoaneurysm formation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: gastric artery injury resulting from blunt abdominal trauma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old woman was brought to hospital in shock after a vehicle collision with upper abdominal pain. Initial contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated liver and splenic injuries along with intra-abdominal hemorrhage and extravascular contrast leakage suspected from the right gastric artery. Angiography showed irregularities of the right gastric artery without active bleeding. Coil embolization of the right gastric artery was performed to prevent rebleeding. The patient subsequently recovered without sequelae and resumed daily activities.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated intra-abdominal hemorrhage and extravascular leakage from suspected right gastric artery injury.
Clinical presentation included shock with upper abdominal pain following blunt trauma.
Angiography showed vessel irregularities in the right gastric artery without active bleeding; coil embolization performed.
The patient recovered fully, resuming daily activities without sequelae post treatment.
